title: Dymphna (15 May)
hookLine: a young Irish princess of legend, patron of those with mental illness

cards: Some saints come to us with letters and records. This one comes to us almost entirely as a story. A king's daughter in Ireland.
Her mother dies, and her father's grief turns into something dark and wrong. The girl runs. With an old priest, she crosses the sea and hides in a small town in what is now Belgium.
Her father follows. The story ends badly, and quickly. But that's not where it stops.
Something grows up around her grave.

teach.h: A SAINT KNOWN MOSTLY BY STORY.
teach.b: Dymphna comes to us as a legend, and historians can't confirm much of it. The Church keeps her as a saint of tradition.
In the legend, she flees with a priest named Gerebernus to Geel. Her father finds them there, and both are killed.

teach.h: A TOWN THAT TOOK PEOPLE IN.
teach.b: Tradition says that people suffering in mind began coming to pray at her shrine, and kept coming. And here's what grew. The town didn't send them away.
The families of Geel began taking them in, as boarders, living in their homes, eating at their tables. Not locked away.
Living alongside. The custom lasted, and Geel is still known for it. So a girl who ran from a household that had gone wrong became the patron of people whose own minds feel like a house gone wrong.
Catholics turn to Dymphna for anxiety, depression and illnesses of the mind, for themselves and for people they love. Her story doesn't promise a quick cure.
It offers company, the kind Jesus promises in Matthew's Gospel, in the Douay-Rheims: "Come to me, all you that labour, and are burdened, and I will refresh you."
Some Catholics pray to her alongside doctors and medicine, not instead of them. The legend is dark. What it left behind is a town that opened its doors.

how: Catholics ask Saint Dymphna's prayers for people living with anxiety, depression and other mental illness; her feast is kept on 15 May in some places, and some hospitals and ministries carry her name.

games.q: you live in Geel. strangers troubled in mind keep arriving to pray at the shrine, with nowhere to stay. what do you do?
o: ask the town to turn them away.
take one of them into your home.
leave it to the shrine's keepers.
games.why: tradition says the families of Geel took them in, to live and eat with them, a custom that lasted.

practice: Bring one person to mind who is anxious, or low, or exhausted inside, maybe someone you love, maybe you, and don't try to fix anything; just keep them company, the way the families of Geel did.

If you pray, ask Saint Dymphna to pray for them; if you don't, simply hold them in mind with kindness. And if you're the one struggling right now, reaching out to someone you trust, or to a doctor, belongs in this too.

wordCard.voice: Dymphna. The young princess of Irish legend who fled to Geel, honored as patron of people who suffer in mind.

carryVoice: Your line: for the troubled mind. What Geel offered was company, not a quick fix. See you tomorrow.
